verdicts.quoted_span: General Laws c. 40P, § 2, "broadly prohibits any regulatory scheme based upon or implementing rent control."
verdicts.reason: The SJC opinion describes a statewide Massachusetts statutory ban on rent control. That ban bars municipalities such as Cambridge from limiting rent increases, and the initiative petition to repeal it was kept off the ballot.

No Cambridge document addresses security deposits. The retrieved security-deposit statute text (D052) describes rules that exist rather than their absence, and that passage does not clearly identify its jurisdiction. Nothing establishes that no rule applies.

DX13 (a secondary source) says Massachusetts law (MGL Ch 186 §15B) forbids landlords from charging application fees. That describes a restriction that exists, not the absence of a rule, so the documents do not support no_rule.

verdicts.quoted_span: The policy order directs the city manager work with relevant city departments to draft policy options or ordinance language that will be presented back to council later this term.
verdicts.reason: The council has only passed a policy order "initiating steps" toward a ban, and the ordinance language is still to be drafted. This indicates that no algorithmic rent-setting rule is currently in effect in Cambridge.
